articles.title: Los 5 ejercicios de fuerza sin impacto con los que se ha preparado Jessica Biel para su nueva película son el mantenimiento perfecto a partir de los 40
articles.summary: Analizamos con un experto el entrenamiento con el que la actriz ha conseguido volver a los rodajes de acción y, como ha dicho ella misma, volver a sentirse c...
articles.body:
Jessica Biel está imparable. La actriz ha reconocido que haber rodado una peli de acción 10 años después de haberlo hecho por última vez ha sido gratificante. "Después de 11 años me siento como antes, lo cual suena increíble", ha confesado a la revista People . La actriz ha coprotagonizado Matchbox: la película , que se estrenó el 9 de octubre en Apple TV y ahora, en plena promoción del largo, ha compartido un video tan tierno como empoderador con su comunidad virtual.

En este la vemos algunos de los ejercicios con los que se ha preparado para las escenas más retadoras bajo las directrices de Ben Bruno, un conocido entrenador personal y preparador físico estadounidense con base en Los Ángeles, graduado con honores Summa Cum Laude por la Universidad de Columbia. Se enfoca en rutinas de fuerza funcionales, sencillas, seguras y eficientes para personas con poco tiempo, priorizando la protección articular y la resiliencia frente a lesiones.

El entrenamiento de fuerza sin impacto de Jessica Biel

El entrenador personal Antonio Pastor Barrón, conocido en redes como @Chiquitrainer, CEO de @we.are.personal ( y en manos de quien se han puesto rostros conocidos como Eugenia Silva , nos ha ayudado a analizar el entrenamiento de Jessica para esta película. Los ejercicios que ha compartido la también directora, de 44 años, que además es mamá de dos niños de 11 y 6, son los siguientes.

Según Chiqui, "es un ejercicio en el que mantenemos la posición de sentadilla apoyados en la pared , sin movimiento. Trabaja principalmente los cuádriceps y mejora la resistencia muscular de las piernas . Es interesante para desarrollar la capacidad de mantener un esfuerzo durante un tiempo prolongado".

En palabras de nuestro experto, la sentadilla búlgara con mancuernas "es un ejercicio unilateral, en el que trabajamos una pierna cada vez. Implica principalmente glúteos y cuádriceps , y ayuda a desarrollar fuerza, estabilidad y control, además de permitir identificar posibles diferencias entre ambas piernas".

Zancada lateral con mancuerna y banda elástica

Nuestro entrenador nos cuenta que "introduce un desplazamiento lateral que trabaja glúteos, muslos y musculatura estabilizadora de la cadera . Es interesante porque no todos los movimientos que hacemos en la vida diaria o en el deporte se producen hacia delante: también necesitamos fuerza y control lateral ".

Puente de glúteos con los pies elevados en suspensión

Chiqui nos cuenta que este ejercicio "trabaja principalmente los glúteos y la extensión de cadera , con una demanda adicional de control y estabilidad. La musculatura de esta zona es importante para caminar, correr, saltar y realizar diferentes movimientos del tren inferior".

Tal y como nos ha confirmado nuestro entrenador, "estos ejercicios implican la musculatura abdominal y otros músculos que ayudan a controlar la posición del tronco y la pelvis. El objetivo es mejorar la estabilidad y la capacidad de mantener una buena posición mientras nos movemos".

Según Chiqui, aunque lo que ha compartido Jessica no es una rutina completa y concreta sino la mezcla de varios ejercicios que ha hecho para prepararse para su nueva película, sí se puede confirmar que ha priorizado el trabajo de fuerza . "No se trata únicamente de tener un físico determinado, sino de desarrollar fuerza, control corporal y tener capacidad para repetir esfuerzos, porque, al final entiendo que muchas de las escenas las va a tener que repetir hasta que salgan bien. Así que la resistencia, la movilidad y la coordinación también son importantes", dice el experto.

Ahora bien, el experto asegura que cualquier mujer debería introducir este tipo de ejercicios en sus rutinas. " Esto no va de que ella sea actriz o de que esté haciendo una película de acción ", dice. Y recuerda que los ejercicios que hace ayudan a "mejorar la capacidad para realizar las tareas del día a día, a mantener la autonomía y a ganar confianza en el movimiento". Esto tampoco quiere decir que cualquiera pueda copiar la rutina de Jessica. Para Chiqui, " es importantísimo adaptar los ejercicios al nivel de cada persona ".

Por otro lado, hay que tener en cuenta que Jessica sufrió una lesión de espalda durante el rodaje, aunque leve. Por eso, su entrenador, Ben Bruno, tuvo que ajustarle la rutina para que pudiera entrenar con la misma intensidad sin hacerse más daño . Esto nos lleva a poner el acento en otro de los recordatorios que nos ha hecho nuestro experto. "Contar con una valoración profesional cuando sea necesario es indispensable".

La película, una aventura llena de acción y viajes por el mundo inspirada en los emblemáticos juguetes de Mattel, se puede ver ya en Apple TV. La historia sigue a un grupo de amigos de la infancia cuyas vidas dan un giro inesperado cuando Sean (John Cena), el cabecilla de la pandilla y ahora agente secreto de la CIA, regresa a la pequeña ciudad tras una larga ausencia. Sin darse cuenta, el grupo se verá envuelto en una frenética persecución internacional para salvar el mundo .

articles.title: La estrella de los '80 que desapareció de la actuación tras casarse con el hijo de James Bond
articles.summary: Mia Sara parecía tener por delante una prometedora carrera en Hollywood, pero la actuación no la hacía feliz y decidió darle un giro a su vida.
articles.body:
Mia Sara parecía tener por delante una prometedora carrera en Hollywood después de protagonizar junto a Matthew Broderick el clásico de los años 80 Un experto en diversión (Ferris Bueller's Day Off) , pero no tardó mucho en darse cuenta de que la interpretación no era el camino profesional que quería seguir.

Desde su matrimonio con el hijo de una leyenda de James Bond hasta su inesperado regreso a la gran pantalla, sigue leyendo para descubrir qué fue de Mia Sara…

La actriz, que interpretó a Sloane Peterson en la exitosa película, continuó apareciendo en algunas películas y series de televisión. Dio vida a Harley Quinn en la serie Birds of Prey y protagonizó junto a Jean-Claude Van Damme la película de ciencia ficción de 1994 Timecop. Sin embargo, después de participar en el cortometraje Pretty Pretty, Sara se tomó un descanso de Hollywood que duró una década. La actriz explicó que la interpretación nunca la hizo feliz.

"Nunca tuve realmente la fortaleza necesaria para afrontar el proceso de las audiciones", confesó. "Hay aspectos de mi carrera de los que estoy muy orgullosa, pero, en general, no fue una carrera que me hiciera feliz". En lugar de continuar actuando, decidió dedicarse a la poesía.

Mia conoció en 1995 a Jason Connery , hijo de la leyenda de James Bond Sean Connery. Ambos trabajaron juntos en Bullet to Beijing y se casaron al año siguiente. Su hijo, Dashiell, nació en 1997, pero la pareja se divorció en 2002.

Más tarde, la estrella de Birds of Prey se enamoró de Brian Henson, hijo de Jim Henson, creador de The Muppet Show. La pareja tuvo una hija, Amelia, en 2005, se casó en 2010 y continúa junta en la actualidad.

Aunque Mia ha dicho que la actuación no es una profesión que la haga feliz, en 2024 regresó a la gran pantalla con La vida de Chuck (The Life of Chuck). A sus 59 años, interpretó a Sarah, la abuela del personaje de Tom Hiddleston, Charles "Chuck" Krantz.

Y no ha descartado volver a trabajar como actriz en el futuro , especialmente si eso implica volver a trabajar con el director Mike Flanagan.

La "muy buena vida" de Mia en Inglaterra

Aunque Mia y su marido son originarios de Nueva York, se mudaron a una casa de campo del siglo XVII en Suffolk, Inglaterra, donde disfrutan de una vida tranquila y alejada de los focos.

"Leo muchas novelas policíacas. Cocino mucho", contó Sara a People. "Empecé cuando era muy joven y, cuando conocí a mi marido, pensé: 'creo que necesito hacerme una vida'. Y conseguí una realmente, realmente buena".

articles.title: Who is Elizabeth Holmes? Nathan Fielder's movie 'You Can See Everything' puts her back in the spotlight.
articles.summary: The former Theranos CEO granted filmmakers extensive access to a project that was kept largely secret for almost four years.
articles.body:
Elizabeth Holmes, the founder of blood-testing startup Theranos, is the subject of a new documentary from comedian Nathan Fielder and filmmaker Lance Oppenheim.

You Can See Everything is in theaters now after being made largely in secret over nearly four years. The movie has already won widespread acclaim , with some critics calling it one of the year's best movies.

Holmes founded Theranos at 19 and became a celebrated Silicon Valley entrepreneur by claiming the company had developed technology capable of performing a wide range of medical tests using a small amount of blood.

But the technology did not live up to her claims, and in 2022, Holmes was convicted of defrauding Theranos investors. She is serving a federal prison sentence.

Filming for the documentary began 34 days before Holmes was due to report to prison, with Fielder moving into her home to capture an unusually intimate look at her life. Here's a look at Holmes's rise and fall.

Holmes founded Theranos in 2003 and served as the company's CEO. Her pitch helped turn her into one of Silicon Valley's most prominent young entrepreneurs. Forbes estimated her net worth at $4.5 billion in 2014, then revised it to $0 in 2016 as Theranos unraveled.

Theranos raised more than $900 million from investors, including media mogul Rupert Murdoch, software billionaire Larry Ellison and the Walton family behind Walmart. The company planned to set up "mini-labs" in Walgreens and Safeway stores, where its small Edison device would provide faster, less invasive blood testing.

Evidence presented at her trial showed that the company's blood-testing technology produced misleading results and that Theranos used conventional laboratory machines for testing that its own technology could not reliably perform.

In 2018, the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) charged Holmes, Theranos and Ramesh "Sunny" Balwani, Holmes's former romantic partner, who served as the company's president and chief operating officer, with raising more than $700 million from investors through what the agency described as a years-long fraud involving false or exaggerated statements about the company's technology, business and financial performance.

Holmes settled the SEC's civil charges without admitting or denying the allegations. She agreed to pay a $500,000 penalty, relinquish voting control of Theranos, return millions of shares and accept a 10-year ban on serving as an officer or director of a public company.

Amanda Seyfried portrayed Holmes in the 2022 Hulu limited series The Dropout , for which she won an Emmy .

A federal jury convicted Holmes in 2022 of one count of conspiracy to commit wire fraud against Theranos investors and three counts of wire fraud against individual investors. The wire transfers involved in those counts totaled more than $140 million, according to the Justice Department .

Holmes was not convicted of defrauding Theranos patients. The jury acquitted her of a patient-related fraud conspiracy charge and three charges involving individual patients. Jurors could not reach verdicts on three additional investor-related charges.

In November 2022, U.S. District Judge Edward Davila sentenced Holmes to 135 months — 11 years and three months — in federal prison, followed by three years of supervision.

Balwani was separately convicted on all 12 criminal charges against him and sentenced to nearly 13 years in federal prison.

Holmes began serving her sentence in May 2023 at a federal prison in Texas, but she is scheduled to move to a halfway house next year.

Holmes has been approved for placement at the Austin Transitional Center in Del Valle, Texas, on Aug. 23, 2027, according to a Department of Justice notification obtained by ABC News .

Her original sentence of 11 years and three months has also been reduced to 10 years and three months. She is now scheduled for release on Feb. 22, 2030. The revised release date reflects a retroactive change to federal sentencing guidelines as well as time earned under the First Step Act.

A federal appeals court rejected Holmes's attempt to overturn her conviction in February 2025 and upheld an order requiring her and former Theranos executive Ramesh "Sunny" Balwani to pay $452 million in restitution.

Holmes told People in 2025 that Evans and their children visit her in prison twice a week. "It kills me to put my family through pain the way I do," she said. "But when I look back on my life, and these angels that have come into it, I can get through anything. It makes me want to fight for all of it."

articles.title: Tom Cruise's 'Digger' is a massive flop. So why can't people stop talking about it?
articles.summary: Some people are delighted to see the film fail. Others are heartbroken. Why has "Digger" inspired such an intense response?
articles.body:
For a moment, before anyone had seen it , Digger seemed like it could be a smash.

Tom Cruise, a perennial box office savior, stars in what was expected to be his first real shot at an Oscar after years of doing his own stunts in crowd-pleasing action movie sequels. It's helmed by Alejandro Iñárritu, a two-time Best Director Oscar winner.

But Digger flopped. It has a 53% rating on Rotten Tomatoes , and is expected to lose $245 million at the box office and come up empty-handed at the Oscars . (Luckily, Cruise nabbed an honorary trophy in 2025 . ) Some bystanders delight in its failure, happy to see big personalities taken down a notch. Others find it troubling that a truly original film has bombed in such a shaky time for the entertainment industry. But none of us can look away.

The plot of Digger is difficult to describe, but I'll take a stab at it: Cruise plays Digger Rockwell, an eccentric and selfish oil magnate whose drilling operation in Greenland causes an environmental catastrophe, sending the other eccentric and selfish personalities of the U.S. government spiraling.

What its trailer hides is a massive twist — a common strategy these days, which worked well for The Drama and Weapons . But that twist is what some people hate most about it.

About half an hour into the movie, it's revealed that we're actually watching the rehearsal of a play about a climate disaster, which really happened in the world of the movie and impacts the daily lives of the actors putting on the show. The rehearsal of Fossil Fools — get it?! — repeatedly halts to insert commentary about the ridiculousness of the money-obsessed men in power, while displaying the difficulties of living in a post-climate-apocalypse hellscape. It makes the film's ultimate message — that we're on the verge of a crisis with fools at the helm — obvious and heavy-handed. I admit I've never seen anything like it before.

That originality, awkward as it may be in this particular film, is rare nowadays. The most bankable movies are consistently built on familiar IP, either sequels to past hits or stories based on books or the lives of extremely famous people. So far in 2026, eight of the top 10 movies at the U.S. box office haven't been original.

Box-office failures have a genuine impact on which movies make it to theaters. Studios don't want to lose millions of dollars for the sake of art, especially not when they're going through $110 billion acquisitions . The Warner Bros. executives who greenlighted other, more successful big swings for auteurs announced they'd be leaving the company just as Digger 's abysmal box office predictions started to trickle in.

Even Ben Affleck has weighed in. "Everybody wants to celebrate this bomb as if it's the most exciting thing to happen. … Everybody wants to count the money, what it lost or whatever," the actor and director told the host of the Happy Sad Confused podcast . "If you punish movies that take risks, guess what you're going to get? A bunch of shitty, homogenized movies. You cannot do something interesting without taking a big swing, and that means you're going to sometimes look bad."

Celebrities like Affleck and Anne Hathaway — both stars who have struck the balance of dominating the box office and earning Oscars — have taken a stand for Digger . "Love the arts. F*** the charts," director (and friend of Iñárritu) Guillermo del Toro posted on X in support of the film.

The prestige swing-and-miss is particularly painful for Cruise, who has gained an enormous amount of public favor in recent years for doing his own stunts and promoting the hell out of the magic of theatergoing. Going from Scientology weirdo who jumped on Oprah's couch to the beloved Mr. Movies is an impressive feat of publicity I'm not sure we've ever seen in the internet era. Though Cruise has been mum on Digger 's box office numbers, it's possible he's not going to take on another risky role anytime soon.

Which is too bad, the film's fans (yes, they exist!) say. M. Cole Chilton, a director and podcaster who loved Digger , tells me that "it's the best film of the year, if not of the century."

"Every scene explains the scene that came before it," he says. "No one could have pulled off the craft of the film other than the most Hollywood actor of all time and the most 'auteur' filmmaker living today."

In Chilton's view, the film is so unique that it was pretty much "doomed the day it started." He's seen the naysayers who seem to be delighting in Digger 's downfall.

So why were so many people seemingly delighted to see it fail? There's a certain schadenfreude to seeing something purposefully pretentious fall flat — especially when it was supposed to be successful.

Lia Baek , a film marketing specialist, says flops "make audiences feel powerful because it proves that attention cannot simply be bought."

"No matter how much money, star power or marketing a studio puts behind a film, audiences still have the final vote," she tells Yahoo. "At the end of the day, audiences decide what becomes culturally relevant. In a way, the flop becomes feedback: If you want us to spend money and go to a theater, you still have to understand what excites us."

To be fair, a lot of people really just didn't like Digger . I didn't, nor did Yahoo's film critic Brett Arnold, who called it "an excruciating, insufferable, direly unfunny and pretentious slog that's self-aware in a way that completely undercuts the entire premise of the movie." That doesn't mean we don't like original movies. It's possible for fresh ideas to make a lot of money at the box office and be genuinely good — just look at Ryan Coogler's Sinners, Kane Parsons's Backrooms or Curry Barker's Obsession.

Even as it prematurely leaves theaters , Digger 's story isn't over. There are still huge swaths of people talking about it, even if half of critics hated it and most people didn't see it. The film has earned itself an online fan army on X, where people with shovel emojis in their display names sing the film's praises , make memes about seeing it and write fanfiction about imagined happenings in Digger 's universe.

Some of the people posting about Digger seem to be doing so ironically . It reminds me of what happened a few months ago with One Night Only , the " sex purge " romantic comedy that bombed despite countless X posts imagining what the dystopian rules for intercourse might be.

Word-of-mouth praise for the critically lauded Obsession made it into 2026's biggest box office phenomenon, but we've yet to see ironic posts lift a bad movie to success — though memes may have briefly brought the awful vampire Marvel movie Morbius back to theaters in 2022. The tongue-in-cheek discussion of Digger 's on-the-nose messaging makes it all seem kind of brilliant in retrospect , as if it's a movie that must be seen repeatedly to be understood , and those who get it are part of a secret exclusive club of elite movie comprehenders .

Online discourse can genuinely turn movies into cult classics , like Jennifer's Body and Babylon . They become more appreciated over time, and their legacies far outlast the initial failed reception. If the real reason people were rooting for Digger is the advancement of art, that's a win. We might need to rely on Mario and Spider-Man to keep theaters in business, though.

articles.title: Vozinha sorprende a Grupo Frontera en concierto y el momento se vuelve VIRAL por el curioso diálogo
articles.standfirst: El portero caboverdiano vive un momento complicado con Colo Colo
articles.summary: El portero caboverdiano vive un momento complicado con Colo Colo
articles.body: La banda mexicana Grupo Frontera mantiene su gira por Sudamérica y en días recientes se presentaron en la Arena Santander, en la ciudad de Santiago, para ofrecerle al público chileno lo mejor de su repertorio junto con algunas novedades en la gira "Triste, pero bien cabrón Tour". Sin embargo, ahora fueron ellos quienes se llevaron una grata sorpresa al ver a Vozinha entre el público. El arquero de Colo Colo y de la Selección de Cabo Verde fue reconocido por Adelaido Solís, vocalista de la banda mexicana durante su presentación en Chile. Al percatarse de su asistencia, el "Payo" no dudó en saludarlo junto con la ovación del público presente que, en caso de haber aficionados de Colo Colo, se olvidaron por un momento de su paso con el cuadro de Fernando Ortiz y brindarle un estruendoso aplauso en plena función. El concierto de Grupo Frontera en la Arena Santander había recorrido más de la mitad de su playlist. Sin embargo, dice que 'más vale tarde que nunca' en un momento viralizado cuando Vozinha fue visto por los artistas y en ello el "Payo" Solís bajó del escenario para anunciar la presencia del portero mundialista, quien estaba instalado en primera fila. Al reconocerlo, el cantante saludó afectuosamente al guardameta, diciéndole: "¡Cómo estás, compadrito!". “No sabía que estabas ahí, hasta que bajé”: fue el curioso diálogo entre el vocalista de Grupo Frontera y Vozinha. El gesto fue discreto, llamando la atención del público presente y otorgándole una ovación al futbolista de Colo Colo, algo que sorprendió al mismo caboverdiano. Tras dicha interacción, al término del concierto el veterano portero pudo compartir minutos en camerinos con la agrupación de origen estadounidense que se dedica a cultivar la música regional mexicana. Vozinha llamó la atención con sus grandes atajadas en el Mundial de Norteamérica 2026 y su desempeño fue del agrado del Colo Colo para ficharlo por un semestre. Sin embargo, el caboverdiano busca inspiración para retomar su mejor nivel, con el que deslumbró en el verano pasado. El guardameta vive meses decisivos y tiene hasta diciembre para cumplir con las exigencias que establece la cláusula del contrato que firmó con los albos para extender la relación por un año más. El rendimiento del guardameta no termina de convencer a Fernando 'Tano' Ortiz quien lo relegó a la banca en el duelo ante Coquimbo Unido. Sin embargo, su fama sigue intacta al ser saludado por agrupaciones y personalidades en todo el mundo. Esa condición tiene un costo, que el portero albo reconoció hace poco en una sentida entrevista, y también beneficios. El más cercano es comercial: acaba de convertirse en embajador de Adidas, por lo cual su estabilidad económica no corre riesgo, pero su lugar en el futbol chileno pende de un hilo.

articles.title: Tiny Desk de Los Tigres del Norte desata polémica: recortan mensaje de apoyo a los migrantes
articles.standfirst: La presentación de Los Tigres del Norte en Tiny Desk quedó envuelta en controversia por la eliminación de una introducción sobre la comunidad migrante en Estados Unidos.
articles.summary: La presentación de Los Tigres del Norte en Tiny Desk quedó envuelta en controversia por la eliminación de una introducción sobre la comunidad migrante en Estados Unidos.
articles.body: La música de Los Tigres del Norte volvió a encontrarse con una de las causas que han marcado su trayectoria: la defensa de los migrantes. Sin embargo, su participación en Tiny Desk de NPR quedó rodeada de polémica después de que circulara una introducción que, según denuncias difundidas en redes sociales, fue retirada de la versión publicada del concierto. El discurso abordaba la situación de la comunidad migrante en Estados Unidos y recordaba episodios históricos de discriminación. El fragmento atribuido a la presentación no cuestionaba la música del grupo, sino que reconocía su importancia para millones de personas que han encontrado en sus canciones una representación de sus experiencias. La controversia surgió cuando usuarios señalaron que esas palabras no aparecían en la edición difundida, lo que abrió interrogantes sobre la decisión de recortar una intervención con un mensaje social. La introducción difundida en redes sociales comenzaba con una afirmación contundente: El discurso mencionaba 1848, año relacionado con los cambios territoriales derivados de la guerra entre México y Estados Unidos, y la llamada Operación Wetback, una campaña de deportaciones desarrollada en 1954. También señalaba que estas políticas y acontecimientos históricos han contribuido a deshumanizar a las comunidades afectadas. El mensaje terminaba reconociendo que Los Tigres del Norte han ayudado a devolver esa humanidad mediante su música, antes de presentar a la agrupación. La relación entre Los Tigres del Norte y la comunidad migrante se ha construido durante décadas mediante corridos que retratan la separación familiar, el trabajo y la búsqueda de oportunidades. Entre las canciones que reflejan esa identidad destacan: Por ello, la introducción difundida encajaba con una trayectoria musical que ha convertido a la agrupación en referente cultural para varias generaciones. La controversia se centra en la ausencia del discurso dentro de la versión del Tiny Desk señalada por los usuarios. En redes sociales circuló una denuncia que aseguraba que la introducción había sido borrada y pedía no olvidar la historia de la comunidad migrante. Sin embargo, la eliminación de un fragmento no demuestra por sí sola que existiera censura política. Para establecerlo sería necesario conocer las razones editoriales de NPR y confirmar las diferencias entre la grabación original y la publicación final. Hasta contar con esa explicación, el motivo del recorte permanece sin aclararse. La discusión, no obstante, trasciende el concierto: vuelve a colocar sobre la mesa la importancia de la memoria histórica y el papel de la música mexicana como voz de quienes viven lejos de su país.

articles.title: In 2005, Leonardo DiCaprio purchased private Belize island for USD 1.75M to create an eco-resort; years later, the project is still under development
articles.summary: Explore the journey of Leonardo DiCaprio's eco-resort project on Blackadore Caye in Belize, facing delays, community pushback, and ongoing development challenges since its purchase in 2005.
articles.body: Over the years, Leonardo DiCaprio has done his part for the community and invested in multiple efforts and organizations that are working towards preserving nature and historical spaces. This was also his main aim when he purchased a private island that is located in Belize, known as the Blackadore Caye, for USD 1.75 million.Here is a look into all that has happened with the property since then.Leonardo DiCaprio once purchased an entire private islandLeonardo DiCaprio purchased the 104-acre Belizean island of Blackadore Caye in 2005 for a reported USD 1.75 million, alongside business partner and resort owner Jeff Gram. At the time, the actor’s initial goal with the private island had been to transform it into a premier eco-resort that would serve as a model for "restorative development," a concept that was intended to heal damage already done to the local ecosystem rather than merely minimizing harm.To make his plans a reality, DiCaprio partnered with luxury developer Paul Scialla to design Blackadore Caye: A Restorative Island.More features about Leonardo DiCaprio’s private resortThe actor aimed to have the entire space powered entirely by solar panels, rainwater harvesting systems, and zero-waste waste-management tech. The main aim of the project was also to preserve the ecosystem on the island, especially the mangroves, which are a vital part of Belize’s ecosystem. Blackadore Caye had reportedly experienced erosion, vegetation loss, and other ecological pressures.The actor had planned on planting thousands of native mangroves, restoring coastal marine life, and building artificial reefs to control coastal erosion caused by historical overfishing and deforestation. Another part of the project was to ensure that around 58% of the island was meant to remain untouched as a form of protected land to ensure that the property that they were building did not affect the flora and fauna of the island too much.The building itself was meant to have 68 guest villas and private residences that were specially designed to meet rigorous LEED and Living Building Challenge sustainability standards.Leonardo DiCaprio’s Belize project has faced a lot of issues and delaysOver the years, the eco-friendly resort has faced quite a few issues. The initial plan had been to launch the property by 2018; however, due to multiple delays and other issues, the Belize eco-friendly resort still remains under construction and development.Some of the issues that ‘The Great Gatsby’ actor faced while working on the project included pushback from local fishermen and activists. At the time when the first drafts for the villas were pitched, local Belizean fishing guides and environmental groups had objected to the project, warning that overwater construction would disrupt shallow-water seagrass beds and threaten key marine life (such as bonefish, tarpon, and permit) vital to the local fly-fishing tourism economy. They claimed that rather than building a sustainable space, some of the structures on DiCaprio’s property would disrupt local wildlife.Due to constant pushback and consultations, the actor had to remove the overwater structures and significantly scale down the master plan, causing extensive regulatory delays. Redeveloping plans took years and delayed the project even further, and the logistics of delivering heavy building materials to a remote island without damaging fragile coastal waters also presented high operational hurdles.As of right now, there is no saying as to when and if DiCaprio’s project will come to completion.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Inside Kapil Sharma’s Dubai cafe: Rs 800 Pani Puri, Rs 500 chai and pretty-in-pink interior
articles.summary: Comedian Kapil Sharma launched his first Kap’s Cafe in Canada in July last year, and the brand has since crossed into the Middle East.
articles.body: Comedian Kapil Sharma launched his first Kap’s Cafe in Canada in July last year, and the brand has since crossed into the Middle East. Its Dubai outlet opened in Al Kifaf on December 31, 2025. Fellow comedian Bharti Singh recently stopped by the new location, which is styled in soft pink and white with refined gold touches.Prices that turn heads at Kap’s CafeKap’s Cafe serves a wide spread of food and drink, from beverages and designer cakes to Indian and international fare. It’s the pricing that grabs attention, though: a cup of masala chai goes for more than Rs 500, and a plate of desi pani puri is Rs 800. Penne pasta tops the menu at Rs 1,604, while the most affordable item, an espresso, still costs Rs 490.Comfort food with premium tags at Kapil Sharma’s cafeThe menu at Kap’s Cafe blends Indian dishes with global favourites, yet even everyday comfort food carries a premium price. A dosa is priced at Rs 775, and both the Bombay sandwich and avocado toast cost Rs 1,034. Sev puri comes in at Rs 905, while French toast is Rs 1,300.Desi favourites get a luxe spin at Kap’s CafeDiners can also order Mexican bowls, butter chicken and pancakes. An aloo paratha is listed at Rs 700, and dal makhani at Rs 1,035. Two items that particularly catch the eye are masala chai at Rs 550 and pani puri at Rs 800, both giving well-loved Indian staples a premium price.Kapil Sharma’s cafe gets a Parisian patisserie lookThe cafe takes its design cues from a Parisian patisserie, combining pastel-pink interiors with ivory touches, white marble and gold accents. This carefully matched colour scheme lends the space a plush, photo-ready charm.Shooting incidents at Kapil Sharma’s Canada cafeLast year, Kap’s Cafe also drew attention for a string of shootings at its Canadian outlet. The café was reportedly fired upon soon after it opened, and was hit again in August. In October, a drive-by shooting reportedly broke the glass front of the premises. A few reports tied the attacks to the Lawrence Bishnoi gang, but these claims were never independently confirmed. Nobody was hurt in any of the incidents.Kapil Sharma reacts to the attacksSpeaking about the attacks in November, during promotions for his film 'Kis Kisko Pyaar Karoon 2', Kapil appeared unshaken by the setbacks. He told the media, “After every firing incident, we got a bigger opening at the cafe. So it is all ok if God is with me.”Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: 'Whalefall' Review: Austin Abrams is swallowed by a sperm whale in immersive survival drama
articles.summary: Fox News Digital reviews 20th Century Studios' "Whalefall" starring Austin Abrams, Josh Brolin, John Ortiz and Elisabeth Shue. Directed by Brian Duffield.
articles.body: Talk about a nightmare come to life. If you have an overwhelming fear of the ocean or being eaten by a whale, perhaps "Whalefall" isn't for you. But if you can stomach, well, being in the stomach of one of Earth's biggest mammals for about 90 minutes, you're in for a whale of a time. "Whalefall," adapted from the 2023 novel by Daniel Kraus, follows Jay Gardiner (Austin Abrams), a college student haunted by the passing of his cancer-stricken estranged father Mitt (Josh Brolin). Mitt, an enthusiastic but erratic scuba diver, had committed suicide by sinking himself in the water off the California coast. ‘THE SOCIAL RECKONING’ REVIEW: ZUCKERBERG, FACEBOOK ARE THE ENEMY IN PREACHY SLOP DISGUISED AS JOURNO DRAMA Feeling guilty about leaving home and not being there for his father's final moments, Jay commits himself to finding his father's remains underwater. However, Jay's search is upended when he's swallowed by a giant sperm whale. For the rest of the film, Jay is literally fighting for his life with less than an hour's worth of oxygen in his tank as he attempts to escape from the belly of the beast, which sometimes involves fighting other creatures, including a giant squid the whale also swallowed. Throughout the ordeal, the film flashes back to his tumultuous relationship with his father. DIGGER REVIEW: TOM CRUISE DESTROYS THE PLANET IN ALEJANDRO IÑÁRRITU'S GRANDIOSE, MESSY POLITICAL SATIRE Austin Abrams has certainly been getting his reps in as a leading man with his other movie, "Resident Evil," still performing well at the box office. There's just something inherently likable about him that will have audiences wanting to root for him, which works in this underdog, truly David vs. Goliath story. Brian Duffield, who previously wrote and directed 2023's alien thriller "No One Will Save You," sure knows how to build suspense with a solo character. What leaves me baffled is how his team brought to life what it's like to be trapped inside a whale. It's difficult to tell where the visual effects end and practical effects and set designs begin. You feel like you're there with Jay. The third act kind of gets lost in the current for me, and 15 minutes of blubber could've been trimmed from the runtime. And why cast someone like Elisabeth Shue to play Jay's mother and then completely underutilize her? ‘PRIMETIME’ REVIEW: ROBERT PATTINSON CHANNELS CHRIS HANSEN IN RIVETING DRAMATIZATION OF ‘TO CATCH A PREDATOR’ CLICK HERE FOR THE LATEST MEDIA AND CULTURE NEWS The Verdict "Whalefall" is a thrilling and immersive survival drama that rides on the tail of Abrams' endearing and heart-wrenching performance and offers promise from Duffield as a rising filmmaker. While this isn't exactly a must-see and not for the faint of heart, this is the type of movie that is best served for the big screen. Whatever you decide, just make sure you come up for air. ★★★ — STREAM IT LATER "Whalefall" is rated PG-13 for peril, violent content, bloody images, some strong language, and thematic content. articles.title: Imran Khan seeks urgent stay on notice to leave India by October 28, moves to Bombay High Court: Report
articles.summary: Actor Imran Khan has approached the Bombay High Court seeking an urgent stay on a notice issued by the Foreigners Regional Registration Office (FRRO),
articles.body: Actor Imran Khan has approached the Bombay High Court seeking an urgent stay on a notice issued by the Foreigners Regional Registration Office (FRRO), which has directed him to leave India by October 28.The petition, filed through advocates Zulfiquar Memon, Parvez Memon and Chirag Naik, described the notice as “arbitrary, unreasoned and wholly misconceived”, arguing that it violates the principles of natural justice as it was issued without giving him an opportunity to be heard. He has also alleged that the action infringes upon his fundamental rights to equality under Article 14 and to life under Article 21 of the Indian Constitution. Khan, who was given two weeks to leave the country, has stated that he has been residing in India since he was two years old. He e-filed his petition on Saturday, the same day the FRRO issued a fresh notice asking him to show cause why action should not be taken against him under the laws governing foreigners and OCI cardholders.Challenging the original notice dated October 14, Khan’s plea termed it a “punitive executive action” and alleged that he was being made a “scapegoat”. It further claimed that the notice appeared to have been issued for “extraneous” reasons to “stifle perceived dissent.”The petition is likely to be mentioned for an urgent hearing on Monday. It also emphasises that the constitutional protections guaranteed under Articles 14 and 21 extend to foreigners residing in India. Khan has argued that the authorities issued the notice without providing reasons or giving him a reasonable opportunity to present his case.The legal challenge comes after Khan was detained during a protest at Mumbai’s August Kranti Maidan on October 10. The demonstration saw participants demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.Through his plea, Khan has sought to quash the FRRO notice and requested that the authorities produce the records and material on the basis of which the decision was taken. He has argued that the notice does not specify the alleged violation and fails to take into account his status as an Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) cardholder.The notice describes Khan as a US national and alleges violations of the Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025, along with the rules and orders framed under it. It also warns of prosecution if he does not leave India within the stipulated deadline.However, Khan’s petition contends that the authorities have not identified the specific provision he allegedly violated or explained when and how the breach occurred. It further argues that the FRRO has considered him only a US national, disregarding the rights associated with his OCI status and his long-standing residence in India.According to the plea, Khan was directed to leave the country within 14 days without a prior inquiry, a show-cause notice or an opportunity to present his case.The petition also challenges the basis of the action, arguing that the protest took place at a venue that was not a restricted area and that OCI cardholders are not barred from participating in demonstrations.Referring to the events leading up to his detention, the plea claims that footage would establish that Khan did not breach any barricades and was in the process of leaving when mediapersons surrounded him. He was subsequently detained by the police along with his partner, Lekha Washington, and cousin, Zayn Marie Khan.Khan has described the direction to leave India as disproportionate, arguing that it would force a lifelong resident to uproot his life over an unproven case involving bailable offences, in which no chargesheet has been filed.In his petition, the actor stated that he has been living in India since he was two years old. He argued that denying interim relief would leave him with no option but to leave the country, his home, family and livelihood.“Such loss cannot be compensated in terms of money or otherwise,” the plea stated.The petition further maintains that the impugned notice does not disclose any security concern or urgency warranting such action. It argues that keeping the notice in abeyance until the petition is heard and finally decided would not prejudice the authorities.The matter follows demands for Khan’s deportation by BJP leader and former MP Kirit Somaiya, who alleged that the actor’s participation in a political demonstration amounted to a violation of immigration rules. Somaiya also called on Mumbai Police to verify Khan’s citizenship status.At the October 10 protest, Khan had said he was attending as a resident of Mumbai and was not representing any political organisation. He also questioned restrictions on freedom of movement and alleged that attempts were being made to silence people.Following his detention, the actor shared a photograph taken inside a police van on social media, captioning it: “Apparently, I am going for a ride.”Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.summary: Alison Arngrim revealed she passed out on her first day filming "Little House on the Prairie" in Simi Valley, and Sean Penn also fainted on set.
articles.body: The cast of "Little House on the Prairie" is opening up about the brutal reality of filming the hit TV series. Cast members were guests on Patrick Labyorteaux's podcast to discuss their experiences on the show. He asked Alison Arngrim, who starred as Nellie Oleson, what the first day was like for her. "Complete chaos and confusion," Arngrim admitted. ‘LITTLE HOUSE ON THE PRAIRIE’ STAR SAYS CHILD ACTORS GET ‘DROPPED’ AFTER HOLLYWOOD FAME FADES She explained that she hadn't known she was supposed to show up with her character's signature ringlet curls, "So it was lots of panic and phone calls back and forth, and then massive curling of my hair. So yeah, bananas. And then, first day on location, of course, I pass out." "So, I was off to just a rousing start right there," she added. The conversation also included fellow cast members Dean Butler, Pamela Roylance and Jennifer Donati, as well as Tracy and Victor French, the children of late cast member Victor French. Labyorteaux also starred in "Little House on the Prairie" as Andy Garvey. During a later conversation about how hot it was in Simi Valley, where the show was filmed, Arngrim joked that the cast and crew were able to tell when summer hit because the "first day of summer is when Alison hits the ground, because I was out like that. It was that hot." LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS Speaking again of her first day on set, she explained that she was "so disciplined," she approached the director and said, "Excuse me, I think I'm going to faint" before she "completely lost consciousness and dropped." "It's like basically how to not pass out was the challenge," she continued. "It was insane, though – the great thing is that other people began to pass out, so people realized it wasn't me, the first one being Sean Penn." Penn, who was a child at the time, "didn't wake up and come back to work. That was it, he was done for the day." She recalled one of these shoots when Charlotte Stewart, who played school teacher Eva Beadle Simms, "was just sitting there, and she had in fact lost consciousness and fainted and blacked out, but just didn't fall over, and they didn't know she was out." About the sweltering set, Butler admitted, "You just had to do whatever strategy you could. articles.title: John Goodman admits he felt 'frightened' after the  sudden fame he experienced from 'Roseanne'
articles.summary: John Goodman admitted he was his "own worst enemy" when fame hit after "Roseanne," sharing how the shift from actor to celebrity shook him deeply.
articles.body: John Goodman is getting real about the downside of starring in one of the biggest sitcoms of all time. During a conversation with the SAG-AFTRA Foundation, the 74-year-old actor admitted he was "frightened" by the level of fame he achieved following his starring role in "Roseanne" and other projects. When asked what his biggest pitfalls were that he wished he would have foreseen, he replied he wished he would have understood fame better. "I wish I would have taken to it better," he said. "I didn't. I was frightened … I'm my own worst enemy, by far." ROSEANNE BARR HASN’T SPOKEN TO TV SISTER LAURIE METCALF SINCE SHOW’S CANCELLATION Earlier in the conversation with interviewer Joe Neumaier, Goodman was asked about the way his career picked up in the late ‘80s and early '90s, and how he shifted from being a more independent actor to being a celebrity. "It changed ,'" he said. "That's when I was told, ‘You better get a publicist and get a hold of this stuff.’ And I just … I had a bad time dealing with how famous I got all of a sudden, and just [said], ‘Well, that ain’t me.'" He added, "It took a long time to deal with it, so I got that out of the way. But just the negotiations you have to go through, the things you have to do to sell a film, they're not ideal, but they need to be done. People put a lot of money into these things, and let's help each other out and get this done. They have a job to do, and you have to support it." At another point in the interview, Goodman shared he agreed to do "Roseanne" "to quit living out of a suitcase," adding that he "hit it off with [Roseanne Barr] immediately, to the point where, and not in an arrogant way, I just knew when I left that I had the job." "Roseanne" aired on ABC for nine seasons from 1988 to 1997, releasing 222 episodes in its first run and winning four Emmy Awards. "At the time, the hot shows in television were all wealth porn, like 'Dynasty,' 'Dallas,' stuff like that. And we were sober reality," he said. "Rose said something early on that 'just because we're poor doesn't make us stupid.' And the reason that family stayed together was because of laughter and obvious love. And I think that showed on the screen in a real way." Following his time on "Roseanne," Goodman starred in many successful movies, including "The Flintstones," "The Big Lebowski," "Monsters Inc." and others, before returning to the role of Dan Conner in the "Roseanne" reboot in 2018. GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE While successful, the reboot only lasted one season, as it was quickly canceled after Barr made a racist statement on social media in reference to President Barak Obama's senior advisor, Valerie Jarrett. Just a few weeks later, ABC announced that the show's cast would be returning for a new spin-off, "The Conners," without Barr. The show aired for 112 episodes from 2018 to 2025, with Goodman filming that and "The Righteous Gemstones" at the same time. "I didn’t think [the 'Roseanne' reboot] was going to go beyond the initial five or six episodes. I thought it’d be a one-off thing, and then we got picked up, and Roseanne got fired," he told The Hollywood Reporter in July 2025. "I thought that was it, and as soon as they dismissed the cast, I picked up 'Righteous Gemstones.' Then we got to do the show again as 'The Conners.' I didn’t know how long it would last, but I sure enjoyed it while I was there." When speaking to the outlet, he also shared that he and Barr had not spoken "for about seven or eight years" at the time, adding "I’d rather doubt if she wants to talk to me." articles.title: 'Days of Our Lives' star Robert Kelker-Kelly ignored alarming symptoms before sudden death: police report
articles.summary: Robert Kelker-Kelly's wife told police the "Days of Our Lives" actor declined a hospital trip despite his alarming symptoms in his final hours.
articles.body: Robert Kelker-Kelly, the actor best known for playing Bo Brady on "Days of Our Lives," experienced chest and arm pain shortly before his death at 62, according to a police report detailing his final hours. The St. Peters Police Department report, obtained by Fox News Digital, stated that Kelker-Kelly's wife, Allison Kelly, told police she picked up her husband, who also worked as a professional pilot, from Spirit of St. Louis Airport at approximately 7:30pm on Oct. 3. During the drive home, Kelker-Kelly said he felt pain in his left arm and chest and asked his wife to pull over so he could vomit, according to the report. ‘DAYS OF OUR LIVES’ STAR ROBERT KELKER-KELLY DEAD AT 62 Kelly asked her husband whether he needed to go to the hospital. He declined and instead requested that she take him home so he could lie down. After arriving at their Missouri residence, Kelker-Kelly changed his clothes and got into bed. He continued experiencing pain and asked his wife to get him an aspirin, according to the report. When Kelly returned from the kitchen, she found her husband unresponsive and not breathing. She called 911 and began performing CPR, according to the report. LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS St. Peters police and the St. Charles County Ambulance District responded to the couple's Missouri home shortly after 8 pm. Paramedics "attempted life-saving measures," but Kelker-Kelly was pronounced dead at 9:09 pm, according to the report. Kelly told investigators her husband had no known medical conditions and took no prescription medications. He had not had any serious injuries or had surgery in the previous year, she said. "Mr. Kelly had reportedly complained of chest pain shortly before becoming unresponsive, and the circumstances appeared consistent with a medical event," police said. articles.title: Salman Khan reveals his nana didn’t speak to his father Salim Khan for 5 years after his parents’ marriage: ‘Not because of religious connotation, he regretted it till he died’
articles.summary: Salman Khan’s parents, legendary screenwriter Salim Khan and Sushila Charak (Salman Khan) had an interfaith wedding.
articles.body: Salman Khan’s parents, legendary screenwriter Salim Khan and Sushila Charak (Salman Khan) had an interfaith wedding. It was a love marriage and the screenwriter has spoken about it at several instances. In the latest episode of ‘Bigg Boss 20 Weekend Ka Vaar’ while praising contestants for standing up against violence inside the house. The actor spoke about a difficult phase in his parents’ relationship, as he revealed that his nana (maternal grandfather) did not speak to his father, Salim Khan after he got married to his daughter.Salman explained that his maternal grandfather was unhappy with his mother’s decision to marry Salim, who was then an aspiring actor trying to make a place for himself in the film industry. He clarified that religion had nothing to do with the disagreement. Instead, his grandfather was worried about his daughter marrying someone associated with the film world. Recalling the reason behind his nana’s objection, Salman said, “Jab mere mata-pita ki shaadi hui, toh usmein koi religious connotation nahi tha. Usmein sirf jo mere nana the, woh is baat se upset the ki yaar, inki shaadi ek good-looking aadmi se ho rahi hai, jo actor banna chah raha hai aur film industry mein hai. Uske upar se aitraaz tha.”He went on to explain that his maternal grandfather was concerned about the environment his daughter would be entering after marriage. “Nana ka yeh tha ki meri beti is mahaul mein kaise rahegi,” Salman recalled, adding that his grandfather maintained his distance from Salim Khan for five years. “Unhone mere papa se paanch saal baat nahi ki,” he said.The rift eventually came to an end after Sohail Khan was born. Salman recalled how his maternal grandfather travelled from Mahim to Bandra carrying a box of jalebis to visit the family. Looking back at the emotional moment, he said, “Tab woh aaye Mahim se Bandra, jalebi ka box leke. Aaye, phir unhone yeh regret dikhaya ki mujhse bahut badi galti hui ki I have missed my grandchildren growing up.”Salman said his grandfather later regretted missing out on his grandchildren’s formative years and the chance to get to know what he described as the “nicest man on earth”. He also remembered the advice his grandfather gave his mother about visiting him, making it clear that she was always welcome but should not return after a fight. Recalling his words, Salman said, “Like that, you can come anytime, lekin jhagda karke tum nahi aaogi.”Salim Khan and Sushila are parents to Salman, Sohail and Arbaaz Khan, as well as daughters Alvira Agnihotri and Arpita Sharma. Salim later married Helen, and in an earlier interview, Salman spoke about how his mother accepted Helen into Salim’s life and how the children gradually embraced her as well. Today, the family shares a warm bond, with Helen being an integral part of their lives.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Engelbert Humperdinck says he tied up a nurse during tuberculosis sanatorium stay after painful treatment
articles.summary: Engelbert Humperdinck revealed on his podcast how he tied up a nurse during his 1961 tuberculosis sanatorium stay after painful daily injections.
articles.body: Engelbert Humperdinck opened up about the time he spent in a sanatorium in 1961. During a recent episode of his podcast, "The Engelbert Humperdinck Show," the 90-year-old British singer recalled his time at Leicester's Groby Road Hospital Sanatorium, after he was diagnosed with tuberculosis. When speaking about the treatments he endured, he described having "to stay on your back for I don't know 8 weeks," without attempting to sit up or "do anything strenuous," in addition to getting "an injection with a needle about this big in your butt" every morning. "There was one lady nurse who was, I don't think she liked me very much because of the injection that she gave me, she really hurt, and I used to scream at her and I used to ask for somebody else. They wouldn't give me anybody else, but this lady was very bad, and she was really hurt, and I had big blue marks," he explained. ENGELBERT HUMPERDINCK SAYS HE ‘WENT THROUGH HELL’ REJECTING 'CASTING COUCH' ADVANCES EARLY IN CAREER After she continued to hurt him with every injection, Humperdinck thought to himself, "When I'm a little better I'm going to do something" and be a bit "mischievous" to get back at her. "I said to my friend in the next bed, I said, 'I've got to get some rope. I get some rope,'" he said. articles.title: Eminem Defends New Collaboration With ‘Old Friend’ Kid Rock: ‘Not About Choosing Sides’
articles.summary: "Just choosing to make music," rapper says of appearing on "Heal My Faith" off Rock's faith-based LP
articles.body:
Eminem defended his guest verse on Kid Rock's new faith-based album , saying their long friendship overshadowed their political divide.

Rock released his new LP Halfway 2 Jesus on Friday, with Slim Shady — a fellow Detroit native and longtime friend of the rocker — appearing on the track "Heal My Faith."

The collaboration drew some criticism from some of Eminem's fans who were taken aback that the rapper — who publicly endorsed Kamala Harris at a Detroit rally in 2024 and has been critical of Trump on tracks like " Campaign Speech " — could collaborate with Kid Rock, perhaps Trump's biggest (and most relevant) supporter in the music industry.

As Eminem explained on social media hours after Halfway 2 Jesus was released, "Not about choosing sides, just choosing to make music with my old friend. Praying for all of us."

Kid Rock elaborated on the collaboration in an interview with Billboard , revealing that while Eminem was first announced as a guest on the song "7 Sins," the rapper instead appeared on "Heal My Faith," the song Rock initially recruited him for. "We agreed we didn't need two songs together…people are going to think we're dating," Rock said.

"We've been friends for, like, 40 years. I really didn't want to drag him into my political world…. We talk about [politics] a little bit, not a ton. There's a lot of stuff we agree on, and we can have a laugh about what [we don't]. That's why I asked him to write a verse for me."

"From shock rap to the rock rap / My homie and me /He is my brother, not my political enemy," Eminem raps on his verse. "B.O. to the B. / We wrote this for those who believe in G.O. to the D / However you voted or lean / Liberal and evangelical can agree / It's God first, home of the free."

"This [album] is about forgiveness and second chances," Rock told Billboard . "Trying to heal some of the division in our country. I'm just putting a positive message out there in the world… showing a little more grace, trying to kill some of the division."

articles.title: Manifest: From reality TV to Wembley arena in one turbulent year
articles.summary: Turkish girl group manifest on taking their music to a global audience, as they prepare for their first UK concert.
articles.body:
When I first meet Turkish girl group manifest, we're on a boat cruising down the River Thames.

The six band members are clutching Union jack umbrellas as they pose for press photographs and mingle with British pop acts, including K-pop-trained boyband dearALICE.

Netflix cameras are filming the evening for a six-part documentary. The group are in London hoping to build on their success in Turkey and reach an international audience.

Their ambitions come after a turbulent year at home, during which the band were prosecuted for public indecency over their outfits and dance moves during a concert in Istanbul.

A few weeks after their appearance on the boat, I meet the group again at Wembley Arena, where they are preparing for their first UK concert the following night.

As the staging - complete with giant LED screens and the group's logo - is set up around them, the six members rehearse synchronised choreography alongside their back-up dancers.

The group consists of main vocalist Sueda Uluca, lead vocalist Lidya Pınar, sub-vocalist Mina Solak, sub-vocalist and main rapper Zeynep Sude Oktay, lead dancer Hilal Yelekçi and main dancer Esin Bahat.

But Wembley is just the beginning of their ambitions.

"After Wembley, we'll manifest Coachella and other big stages," says Hilal Yelekçi, playing on the group's name.

manifest were formed in February last year through the Turkish reality TV talent competition Big5 Türkiye, which saw contestants compete over several months for a place in the group.

They were mentored by established Turkish pop stars, including Gülçin Ergül, a former member of girl group Hepsi, who was also a judge on the show.

The band's rise has been rapid, and they now have more than six million monthly listeners on Spotify.

While in London, they released their first English-language single, TRALALA, which topped YouTube's daily music video chart on its release, ahead of videos from Shakira and Taylor Swift.

The music video was also their first to be filmed outside Turkey, with the group working with a largely British production crew in east London.

"Getting out from that safe zone was a bit stressful for us," says Pınar.

Despite their hopes to perform on British and American stages, they're keen to retain their Turkish identity.

"We want to reach a global audience with our Turkish songs actually, not with English ones," says Sude Oktay.

"We want to teach people to sing in Turkish."

Alongside Turkish girl group Hepsi, manifest cite the Spice Girls among their musical inspirations.

Pınar says her favourite Spice Girl is Baby Spice.

"Because of the pink. I'm pink and blonde, so it's obvious," she laughs.

They have also had the chance to meet one of the world's biggest pop stars, Dua Lipa.

The British-Albanian singer met manifest backstage before watching them perform at her Sunny Hill Festival in Kosovo in July this year.

"She came to our backstage and said a lot of great things," one member recalls.

"We really love her, her songs, her stage presence."

However, the band's road to success was threatened last year.

The trip to London comes just over a year after Turkish prosecutors launched an investigation into the group over allegations of violating public decency, following criticism of their outfits and choreography at an over-18s concert in Istanbul.

A Turkish court later ruled that their choreography and physical contact on stage amounted to exhibitionism.

In a post on X, Turkish politician Oktay Saral called for action so the group "can never repeat such acts".

The case also prompted criticism over artistic freedom in Turkey, where authorities have previously cancelled concerts and festivals over concerns about public morality.

Turkish singer Ceylan Ertem described the investigation as "an open attack on women's freedom and the performing arts".

The six members were handed suspended prison sentences of three months and 22 days. A ban preventing them from leaving Turkey was also lifted by the court.

Speaking to me in London, the group would not talk about the sentencing. Instead they spoke about wanting to inspire a new generation of Turkish girls.

"We are six different women, we have different hobbies... " says lead vocalist Pınar.

"We really, really want to see that little girls look at us and maybe they want to sing too, they want to dance too.

About 300 fans attended a signing event at a Turkish restaurant in London, giving the group their first chance to meet some of their UK-based supporters in person.

"Our concerts and events have been in Turkey before and we never met them face-to-face," says Pınar.

On the day of the concert, there was a sense of excitement outside Wembley Arena as fans wearing manifest-branded headbands and carrying banners gathered.

The crowd was predominantly Turkish women in their 20s and 30s, many dressed in colours associated with the group.

Among them were friends Elif, 31, and Zeynep, 25, both Turkish women living in London, who reflected on the band's past year.

"I don't think I've ever heard of a girl band performing there," says Zeynep.

"I think I was seven when Hepsi were last together. It's maybe a once-in-a-lifetime experience."

Turkish pop star Tarkan previously performed at Wembley Arena in 2008.

For Elif, the concert has a wider significance.

"We are going through difficult times back home. It means girl power and empowerment, and just having fun and being together," she says.

"I feel like back home people came together to support them and criticise the treatment that they were receiving from the government."

Zeynep hopes the group will one day be able to perform freely in Turkey.

"It's great to see them here, but I hope one day they will be back in Turkey and they'll be able to do whatever they want without getting persecuted for it," she says.

The sense of girl power was strong as the group took to the Wembley stage, opening their set with Hileli before launching into TRALALA.

Throughout the evening the group switched between English and Turkish, at one point asking the audience who was Turkish and who was English. The loudest cheers came from the Turkish fans.

Alongside their own songs, they performed covers of One Direction's Story of My Life, the Spice Girls' Wannabe and the Pussycat Dolls' Hush Hush.

Hush Hush interpolates Gloria Gaynor's I Will Survive, which the group sang in Turkish, a striking moment for a group determined to bring their language to an international audience.

Even though manifest have their sights set on stages around the world, after several weeks in London they were missing some of the comforts of home.

"Turkish food, like kebab," says rapper Sude Oktay, before adding mantı, a traditional Turkish dumpling dish.

"Turkey is our home," says Pınar. "We miss our home."

articles.title: Daniel Lopes junta Noel Rosa, Fausto Fawcett, Jorge Vercillo e IA na pista do álbum 'Já que veio, fica para dançar' | G1
articles.body:
Daniel Lopes (à esquerda) recicla a gravação do samba 'Com que roupa?', feita em 1930 por Noel Rosa (1910 –1937), no fecho do álbum 'Já que veio, fica pra dançar' — Foto: Marcelo Camelo / Reprodução / Montagem g1

♬ Quase um século atravessa a gravação do samba “Com que roupa?” – composto em 1929 e gravado em 1930 pelo autor, Noel Rosa (1910 – 1937) – e a edição do álbum “Já que veio, fica pra dançar”, do compositor, produtor musical e multi-instrumentista carioca Daniel Lopes. Pois a gravação de “Com que roupa?” com Noel é reciclada no arremate do álbum lançado ontem, 16 de outubro, em edição independente do artista.

Residente há três anos em Lisboa, capital de Portugal, Daniel Lopes manda de além-mar um álbum que recorre às ferramentas da inteligência artificial – como na formatação do samba “Eclipse total”, no qual figura o cibernético carioca Fausto Fawcett – sem abrir mão de alguns encontros presenciais entre as conexões digitais.

Se há organicidade no canto de Chico Chico, autor e convidado da canção “E tudo mais”, há IA na criação dos arranjos de músicas como “Amor, mistério e dor”, composição de Luís Carlinhos e Bruno Levinson encorpada com vozes artificiais.

Ao longo das 15 faixas do álbum “Já que veio, fica pra dançar”, Daniel Lopes promove encontros com Anna Ratto (na canção “Quero saber”), Lia Sabugosa – intérprete do hino geracional “Como nossos pais” (Belchior, 1976), lançado há 50 anos – e Jorge Vercillo, presente em “Quatro elementos”, música que se afina pela temática espiritualista com “Paz na terra”, canção composta e interpretada por João Viana.

Já “Moacir in blues” cruza tempo e espaço para conectar o saxofonista Moacir Silva (1940 – 2002) com o neto do músico, o baixista Jorge Ailton.

Antes de migrar para Portugal, onde desenvolve projetos musicais para os mercados europeu e brasileiro, Daniel Lopes foi líder da banda Reverse ao longo dos anos 2000 e integrou o trio Les Pop, com o qual legou um dos grandes discos da cena indie dos anos 2010, “Quero ser cool” (2011), lançado há 15 anos. Paralelamente, Daniel Lopes também construiu discografia solo que rendeu álbuns como “Bonito” (2012) e “Input relâmpago” (2014).

articles.title: Val Chmerkovskiy gets one-week suspension on ‘Dancing with the Stars’
articles.summary: Val Chmerkovskiy will not be participating in the upcoming episode of “Dancing with the Stars.”
articles.body: Val Chmerkovskiy will not be participating in the upcoming episode of “Dancing with the Stars.” The show announced Saturday that Chmerkovskiy, a pro on the competition who is paired with actor Jenna Dewan, will be suspended for a week. It comes after Chmerkovskiy posted a status on TikTok last week that appeared to reference Will Smith’s notorious altercation with Chris Rock at the 2022 Oscars. The pro had been reacting to the harsh critique that judge Carrie Ann Inaba gave his wife, fellow pro Jenna Johnson who is paired up with actor Harry Shum Jr. “You almost saw Fresh Prince enter the ballroom last night,” Chmerkovskiy wrote in the since-deleted status seen by NBC News. In a statement to NBC News, BBC Studios, the production company behind “DWTS,” said that the “well-being of everyone who works on Dancing with the Stars is non-negotiable.” “Val’s social media post was inappropriate and does not reflect the values or standards expected of anyone connected with the show,” the statement said. “As a result, he will not participate in next week’s show.” Chmerkovskiy responded to the news of his suspension by posting an apology to his Instagram story. The dancer wrote that he initially intended to “defend my wife.” “I made a poor decision to reference a meme to ‘keep my wife’s name’ out of the conversation, without stopping to think through what else that reference could imply, which was genuinely never my intention,” he wrote, referencing Smith’s words to Rock amid the Oscars spat, “Keep my wife’s name out of your f-----g mouth.” Chmerkovskiy added: “Carrie Ann certainly didn’t deserve to get caught in the middle of my bad judgment, and I hate that she was.” He also had some well wishes for those on the show. “Please send Carrie Ann, Jenna, and the whole DWTS family lots of love during Dedication Night,” he wrote. “I’ll be watching and cheering everyone on!!” Inaba has not responded publicly to Chmerkovskiy’s apology or suspension. Instead of performing with Chmerkovskiy, Dewan will be dancing with pro Alan Bersten in a number that’s dedicated to her mother. Things got heated on the Tuesday episode of “DWTS” when Inaba accused Johnson of incorporating a lift into her samba routine with Shum. The Latin style of dance traditionally prohibits the move — something that the judge has enforced in the past. While Johnson, looking confused, asked, “Lift?” Inaba returned with an immediate response. “A lift is, I just need to say it,” she said before reading off of a sheet of paper with the printed definition. “Any movement during which one of the dancers has both feet off the floor at the same time with the assistance or support of their partner. Yeah. Lift.” Later on in the episode, Johnson appeared to take the criticism well. “I will take it, sure,” she said. Chmerkovskiy has previously apologized for his TikTok status. On Thursday, he posted on his Instagram story that he had reached out to Inaba directly to apologize. “I recognize that I am in a fortunate position to have a platform and to be a role model to some, and I need to treat that with more care by actively pausing to think before I post to ensure what I am sharing aligns with who I am, and who I want to be for you all,” he wrote in the Instagram story.

articles.title: Colours of Navaratri - Day 8: Purple, with a touch of old-school charm
articles.summary: For singer Swarathmika, Navaratri is a time when she gets to embrace her love for silk saris, temple jewellery and flowers.
articles.body: For singer Swarathmika, Navaratri is a time when she gets to embrace her love for silk saris, temple jewellery and flowers. As she celebrates Day 8 in purple, she talks about why she gravitates towards the colour, her old-school approach to dressing, the singers whose style she admires and her plans to squeeze in kolu visits between a busy schedule of concerts.‘Whenever I wear purple, I feel very calm and composed’Wearing purple provides Swarathmika with a sense of calm. “When I wear purple, I feel very calm and composed. When I wear purple to concerts, I feel I look very presentable. It’s a colour that makes me look bright and suits me well. It also makes me more confident and brave,” she explains.‘My Navaratri fashion is 100 per cent traditional’A traditionalist at heart, Swarathmika believes a well-woven silk sari is a must-have in her Navaratri wardrobe. “My Navaratri fashion is 100 per cent traditional. I’m very old-school. Mostly, I will be in saris during the festival. I don't overdo anything. I love keeping it simple and elegant. Generally, I prefer no makeup and keeping the jewellery very minimal. A gold chain and minimal earrings are more than enough for me," she says. If she had to accessorise a purple sari, she would go for either temple jewellery or kemp jewellery. “Some kemp jewellery comes in purplish shades, so I'd pair it with that. I'd also wear a big necklace and a bunch of glass bangles. And, of course, flowers.”When I wear purple, I feel very calm and composed. It’s a colour that makes me look bright and suits me well. It also makes me more confident and brave‘I like pairing my saris with antique, gold-ish colours’Gold takes precedence over silver when it comes to her jewellery choices. “Since I wear a lot of temple jewellery, I like pairing my saris with antique, gold-ish colours. Almost 99% of my collection is temple jewellery. I wear silver jewellery, but I don't feel it has the completeness of gold,” she says. While she usually keeps her accessories minimal, Navaratri is a time when she wears more bangles. “As I can’t wear many bangles during concert time, I wear a lot of glass bangles during Navaratri,” she says.‘I love wearing flowers, especially purple-coloured flowers’For Swarathmika, no look is complete without flowers, especially if they are purple in colour. “I love wearing flowers, especially purple-coloured flowers. I recently went to the US for my first tour. Even there, I got myself a bunch of artificial flowers. Flowers are very important to me. I don't feel complete unless I keep flowers for all my concerts. Actually, purple reminds me of the December flowers,” she says.‘I admire MLV amma's dark lipstick and makeup; MS Blue and MS Green are iconic’Among the musicians whose style she admires are MS Subbulakshmi and ML Vasanthakumari. “MS Blue and MS Green are iconic. MS amma looked so beautiful even without makeup. I also admire MLV amma's dark lipstick and makeup. She used to light up any place she was in,” she says.STYLE FILEThe silk sari: A purple sari paired with a mustard-yellow blouse, gold jhumkas, jasmine flowers and a traditional bun is a timeless combination.The lehenga: A lilac lehenga with a silver-embellished blouse, pearl accessories, a delicate maang tikka and soft curls will be pretty, dreamy and festive.The churidar: Go for a lavender or deep plum churidar, a delicate silver-embroidered dupatta, oxidised silver jhumkas, and embroidered matching bangles. Add a soft braid with flowers and a small bindi for that effortless, traditional Navaratri vibe.The office look: Opt for a purple crop top with sharara or dhoti pants, a mirror-work jacket, chunky silver earrings and metallic juttisDon't feel like you have to match everything just because you're wearing purple. Play around with mustard yellow, lime green, hot pink, silver or antique goldBEAUTY FILEBase: Hydrating natural base with soft peachy mauve blush makes the look feel fresh. Eyes: Soft brown with lilac or shimmery lavender with a smudged wing will be the best option for eye makeup.Lips: Mauve nude with a plumper glossy lip would work well with a purple sari.Finishing touch: Go for a half-moon bindi with a hydrating finishing spray for a fresh and dewy makeup finish.Pair with a royal purple outfit, antique gold jewellery and an elegant hairstyle for a natural grand look that also gives a traditional feelGet the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Shamna Kasim says Rajinikanth’s ‘Jailer 2’ is a dream come true; ‘We all say that our hard work, prayers, and passion would pay off one day’
articles.summary: Actor Shamna Kasim has expressed gratitude to audiences for embracing her dance appearance in Rajinikanth’s ‘Jailer 2’.
articles.body: Actor Shamna Kasim has expressed gratitude to audiences for embracing her dance appearance in Rajinikanth’s ‘Jailer 2’. The actor also thanked director Nelson Dilipkumar, producer Kalanithi Maran and composer Anirudh Ravichander for giving her the opportunity to feature in the film. In a video shared on social media, Shamna opened up on her experience of being part of a major project featuring the Superstar.Shamna Kasim on sharing screen space with RajinikanthShamna revealed that she has admired Rajinikanth for years and never expected to appear alongside him in a film. She also mentioned ‘Padayappa’ as one of her favorite movies featuring the veteran actor."Everyone would like to share screen space with a style icon such as Rajinikanth sir. I never thought that I would have that opportunity," Shamna said. The actor features in the special song ‘Ala Bolelo’, which also includes Rajinikanth and Suraj Venjaramoodu.Shamna Kasim thanks Nelson DilipkumarShamna said she had been waiting for ‘Jailer 2’ to release so she could thank viewers for their response to the song. She specifically credited Nelson Dilipkumar for recommending her for the appearance."I must thank Nelson sir a lot, because he pitched me for the song," the actor revealed. She also spoke about the excitement of performing in a major production. The opportunity allowed her to be part of a song that audiences are now celebrating in theaters."I never thought that I would be able to do such a good song for three minutes in a big project such as this," Shamna added.The response to ‘Jailer 2’ has been particularly meaningful for Shamna, who described the moment as an example of how perseverance can lead to unexpected opportunities."We all say that our hard work, prayers, and passion would pay off one day. I am going through such days," the actor added.Shamna Kasim shares an emotional note before releaseAhead of the film's release, Shamna shared a lengthy message about her gratitude for the opportunity. She wrote, "And the wait is finally over! I have always dreamt of being a part of a project this huge, and finally, that day is here!"Meanwhile, ‘Jailer 2’ recorded an increase in its domestic collections on Saturday, October 17. According to Sacnilk, the Rajinikanth-starrer earned Rs 47.80 cr in India net collections on its third day. This marked a 28.8% rise from Friday's Rs 37.10 cr. The film's worldwide gross collection reached Rs 317.15 cr within three days of its theatrical release.
